newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha holds steady but end-users incredulous.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha holds steady but end-users incredulous.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices held steady on Thursday after yesterday's strong cargo deal but end-users as expected claimed the fundamentals did not justify higher prices.
Brokers said traders were supporting physical prices and cargo supplies were on the tight side.

NWE cargoes were notionally valued at $186/$187 cif after a trade late Wednesday at $186.75 cif basis Rotterdam for 25,000 tonnes of Egyptian Alex material, for prompt arrival. No deals were heard yet on Thursday.
June swaps were unchanged at $181/$183. July swaps were valued at $179/$180.
But some brokers said the backwardation had widened out to $3.50 to $4 after the cargo trade.
"There is still some buying interest from traders in Northwest Europe," a broker said. "The market looks relatively stable to tight on the cargo side but the end-users are well covered."
A debate continued to boil over whether gasoline's recent weakness was cutting into reformer demand for the heavier napthenic and aromatic (N+A) supply, a feedstock for making gasoline.

An end-user discounted talk that reformers would still buy naphtha and also believed that paraffinic material was valued at $10 below current gasoline barge prices. That would put cargo prices at $180/$181.
"I don't believe in those numbers...For real reforming purposes I wouldn't buy it," he said, referring to the cargo deal at $186.75. "I think we will see a downward trend in the next few days."
He also said barge material in Rotterdam was ample.

According to industry sources, however, naphtha inventories held in independent tankage in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp area fell to 75-100,000 tonnes in the week ending Thursday, from 100-125,000 the previous week. Stocks are up slightly from year-ago levels of 50-75,000 tonnes, the sources said.
The sources said stocks fell as no cargoes arrived and product left by barge to the German chemical sector.
